note.text:
A line segment [AB] is the part of the line (AB) between A and B. A and B are its end points. Its length is written AB, for example AB = 8 cm.
Notation: (AB) is the line, [AB) the half line from A, [AB] the segment, AB its length.
The midpoint M of [AB] is on the segment, halfway between A and B: AM = MB = AB ÷ 2.
A point M is on the segment [AB] exactly when AM + MB = AB. If AM + MB is more than AB, M is not on [AB].
If M is on [AB], then MB = AB − AM.

worked_example.problem: M is the midpoint of [AB] and N is the midpoint of [AM]. AB = {ab} cm. Find AN and NB.
steps: M is the midpoint of [AB], so AM = MB = {ab} ÷ {two} = {ab / two} cm.
N is the midpoint of [AM], so AN = NM = {ab / two} ÷ {two} = {ab / 4} cm.
NB = NM + MB = {ab / 4} + {ab / two} = {3 * ab / 4} cm.
worked_example.answer: AN = {ab / 4} cm and NB = {3 * ab / 4} cm.

cards.idea: A segment is named with square brackets around its two end points. Its length is written with no brackets.
example: [AB] is the segment with end points A and B; AB = {ab} cm is its length.
(AB) is the whole line, and [AB) is the half line from A.

check.prompt: Which one names the segment with end points {L[0]} and {L[1]}?

misconceptions.explain: ({L[0]}{L[1]}) with round brackets is the whole line, which has no end points.
[{L[0]}{L[1]}) is a half line: it starts at {L[0]} and never ends.
{L[0]}{L[1]} with no brackets is the length of the segment, a number of centimetres.

solution: A segment is written with square brackets around both end points.

cards.idea: The midpoint of a segment is on the segment, at the same distance from both end points: half of the length.
example: AB = {ab} cm, M the midpoint of [AB]: AM = MB = {ab} ÷ {two} = {ab / two} cm.

cards.idea: A point M is on the segment [AB] exactly when AM + MB = AB.
example: AB = {ab} cm, AM = {am} cm, MB = {mb} cm: {am} + {mb} = {am + mb} = AB, so M is on [AB].
If AM + MB were more than AB, M would be off the segment.

cards.idea: If M is on [AB], the two parts add up to the whole: MB = AB − AM.
example: AB = {ab} cm and AM = {am} cm, so MB = {ab} − {am} = {ab - am} cm.

questions.prompt: AB = {ab} cm and M is the midpoint of [AB]. Find AM.

misconceptions.explain: AM is only half of AB.
AM is half of AB, not double.

solution: The midpoint is halfway: AM = AB ÷ {two}.

questions.prompt: AB = {ab} cm, AM = {am} cm and MB = {mb} cm. Is M on the segment [AB]?

misconceptions.explain: AM + MB = {am} + {mb} = {am + mb} cm and AB = {ab} cm. {am + mb == ab ? 'AM + MB is equal to AB' : 'AM + MB is more than AB'}.

solution: AM + MB = {am} + {mb} = {am + mb} cm and AB = {ab} cm.
{am + mb == ab ? 'AM + MB is equal to AB' : 'AM + MB is more than AB'}, so the answer is {answer}.

questions.prompt: M is on the segment [AB]. AB = {ab} cm and AM = {am} cm. Find MB.

misconceptions.explain: M is between A and B, so MB is shorter than AB: subtract.

solution: The two parts make the whole: AM + MB = AB.

questions.prompt: M is the midpoint of [AB] and AM = {am} cm. Find AB.

misconceptions.explain: AM is half of AB, so AB is double AM.
AB is the whole segment: AM + MB.

solution: M is the midpoint, so MB = AM = {am} cm.

questions.prompt: A, B and C are on a straight line, in that order. AB = {ab} cm and BC = {bc} cm. Find AC.

misconceptions.explain: B is between A and C, so add the two parts.

solution: B is between A and C, so B is on the segment [AC].

questions.prompt: M is the midpoint of [AB] and N is the midpoint of [AM]. AB = {ab} cm. Find NB.

misconceptions.explain: That is AN. NB goes from N to B: NM + MB.
That is MB. NB = NM + MB.

solution: N is the midpoint of [AM], so NM = {ab / 2} ÷ {two} = {ab / 4} cm.
